page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-96 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor featuring 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with multithreading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 192 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench metrics. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptography acceleration, which contribute to top-tier scores in Passmark extended instructions and encryption tests. Memory performance is strong, with small-block cached read bandwidth exceeding 10,000 GB/sec and large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 328.35 GB/sec.

The high-density compute profile makes the n4d-highcpu-96 highly effective for CPU-bound workloads. It achieves top-tier results in software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. Additionally, it demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, handling 160.69 million Redis SET operations per second, and static web serving. While it lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, its raw CPU capacity and vector instruction support enable efficient execution of high-throughput batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference tasks.
